about: MUTATING — creates or replaces ONE repository ruleset on GitHub that protects the branches matching a pattern, and nothing else (infra/forge/github-act.sh set-branch-protection). Design 76155676 decision 4 (David 2026-09-27: GitHub acts are bounded verbs, plan then passkey-approved write, each proving by reading GitHub back; backlog 6a8ff89f). A ruleset rather than classic branch protection because the classic endpoint takes one branch NAME and cannot carry a pattern such as publish/**. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-github-branch-protection as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders from GitHub and acts only while the bytes hash alike. Its bound is the script's: the verb owns exactly one ruleset per pattern, named `boss: refs/heads/<pattern>`, created (POST) or replaced whole (PUT); it never touches a ruleset it did not name and never deletes one; the rules are FIXED in the script — creation, update (restrict updates), deletion, non_fast_forward, plus required_status_checks when checks are named — so a request chooses only who may push (bypass actors app:<App id> or team:<team id>, or none: nobody) and which checks. A rulesets API has no user actor, so an identity is an App or a team. It authenticates as the GitHub App's INSTALLATION on <owner>, from the slot /etc/boss-publish/github-app/<owner>.token the forge converge renders from the broker's installation token (per-owner data, never a constant); a slot that is absent, loose, not root's, empty or expired is a refusal before GitHub is called, and the token is never printed. Proof: the ruleset reads back, normalised, equal to the plan — one that does not is exit 1. Any other 4xx or 5xx is exit 1 naming GitHub's words.
effect: ^github-act: proven — ruleset .+ reads back as desired
